name: Afonja, Alimi and the fall of Oyo

summary.text: In 1817 Afonja, Oyo’s own commander-in-chief, rose against the Alaafin at Ilorin and called in Shehu Alimi, a Fulani Muslim teacher, and his following of Hausa and Fulani fighters. The alliance cut Oyo off from its north. About 1824 Alimi’s son Abdulsalami turned on Afonja, who was killed, and Ilorin became an emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate under Gwandu. Ilorin’s armies ended Oyo-Ile in the 1830s, and the court moved south to Ago-Oja, today’s Oyo.

moments.title: Afonja’s revolt
moments.text: The Are-Ona-Kakanfo declares Ilorin independent of the Alaafin and invites Shehu Alimi to fight beside him.

moments.title: The allies fall out
moments.text: Abdulsalami, Alimi’s son, turns on Afonja, who is killed. Ilorin becomes an emirate.

moments.title: Oyo-Ile abandoned
moments.text: After defeat by Ilorin, the capital of the old empire is left empty; Oyo is rebuilt far to the south.
